title: Slimline console collector and GraphQL I/O refactor
creator: Marcus Lee
description: Refactor the console backend ingestion and aggregation path to reduce tail latency, memory churn, and unnecessary fanout between the REST ingestion layer and GraphQL resolvers. The current implementation has multiple transformation hops: REST collector -> legacy aggregator -> serializer -> GraphQL hydrator. This ticket consolidates the hot path into a slim, async collector service that emits compact envelope messages and introduces segmented read-through caching with adaptive TTLs. Goals: 1) reduce 95th/99th percentile API latency for dashboard queries by 30% vs current baseline, 2) reduce p95 memory allocations for aggregate requests by 25%, 3) remove a legacy in-process cache adapter and replace it with a sharded, LRU-backed cache with clear eviction signals, 4) keep functional parity with existing dashboards and rollout behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: p95 API latency for typical dashboard query reduced by >=30% in staging compared to baseline (dashboard-load-2025-02-10)
Memory allocations for aggregation worker during 10k qps synthetic test reduced by >=25%
All existing GraphQL fields returned unchanged (no semantic regressions) for canonical prompt sets
New collector can be toggled via runtime feature flag and supports canary routing to 5% of traffic
No new SLO violations introduced for unrelated console routes during rollout
tasks: Profile current hot path and capture allocation/latency flamegraphs (baseline artifacts attached)
Implement async slimline collector that merges REST and GraphQL prefetch logic into a single pipeline
Replace legacy serializer with compact msgpack envelope and version header
Introduce sharded LRU cache with per-shard metrics and eviction hooks
Add adaptive TTL heuristic: short TTL for high-throughput keys, longer TTL for stable summaries
Add integration tests for resolver parity and end-to-end harness against staging data
Create rollout plan: feature flag, 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error rate spike
Update observability: new dashboards for collector latency, cache hit/miss, eviction rate, and memory usage
Add migration note and runbook for rollback and troubleshooting
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created after spike incident during dashboard peak. Initial profiling indicates serializer churn and duplicate fetches across resolvers.
2025-02-21: PoC implemented for msgpack envelope and single-pass prefetch in local environment. Observed ~18% p95 reduction locally.

2025-02-24: Design review completed with API and Platform owners. Decision: preserve GraphQL schema, do not change field semantics. Follow-ups: add exhaustive resolver tests and verify function-calls behavior.
2025-02-27: Sharded LRU cache library chosen (internal fork of lru-shard v2). Security review required for dependency update (opened SNYK ticket).
2025-03-03: Integration tests passing in CI. Canary rollout config prepared. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8421 awaiting reviews.
2025-03-05: Began 5% canary in staging; initial telemetry looks good. p95 reduction at staging observed ~33% on sampled queries. Monitoring for memory regression ongoing.
decisions: Consolidate REST and GraphQL prefetching into one collector to eliminate duplicate fetches and cross-layer serialization costs.
Use compact msgpack envelope (versioned) rather than JSON to reduce serialization CPU and payload size.
Adopt sharded LRU cache with explicit eviction hooks to avoid stale prefix hits; will instrument eviction reasons for later tuning.
Keep GraphQL field-level contract unchanged; collector returns same resolved data shape so clients are unaffected.
Rollout via a runtime feature flag with canary percentages and automated rollback if error_rate > 0.5% or p99 latency regresses by >10%.
Postpone a large dependency upgrade (node runtime) to a separate ticket to reduce blast radius; only upgrade cache lib minor versions now.
risks: Collector consolidation may hide a regression that only appears under full production mix of dashboards and ad-hoc queries
Msgpack versioning mismatch could cause incompatible readers if older workers remain during partial rollout
Cache eviction tuning might temporarily increase cold-miss load and spike upstream datastore QPS
Dependency security review for the chosen LRU shard library may reveal an issue requiring revert
blockers: SNYK security review on sharded-lru fork must complete before GA rollout
Platform team needs to expose feature-flag route for collector routing in dedicated clusters
End-to-end test data scrubbed copy required from privacy team to validate parity on real payloads
next_steps: Complete security review and close SNYK issues or apply mitigations
Monitor canary for 48 hours, collect p95/p99 and memory allocation metrics, iterate on TTL heuristics
Resolve minor feedback from PR #8421 (narrow scope changes requested by platform reviewer), then promote to 25%
Prepare post-mortem style doc capturing lessons and tuning knobs for future aggregation refactors
notes: Keep an eye on hot keys — the adaptive TTL should not increase TTL for high-cardinality metrics.
If msgpack introduces any ambiguity for typed fields, add a versioned compatibility layer to the reader
Consider a follow-up ticket to migrate other aggregators to the same envelope format for cross-service reuse
